messages:
maya: FYI — paging: customers reporting elevated latency and intermittent 5xx on /v1/embeddings (us-west-2) starting ~2026-03-15T10:05Z. I put a quick status-page draft below, pls review and flag wording/legal.

maya: ```
Investigating: Increased latency and errors for embeddings API in US regions
- What’s happening: Some embeddings requests are returning 502/504 or timing out
- Who’s affected: subset of customers using embeddings in US (primarily us-west-2)
- What we’re doing: engineers are investigating routing/capacity; autoscaling and rolling fallbacks being exercised
- Customer impact: degraded performance and intermittent failures for affected requests
- Next update: within 30 minutes or earlier if there’s a significant change
```

emily: Thanks — a few quick edits for public-facing tone: avoid technical rollout details (e.g., "rolling fallbacks"), and don’t assert root cause. Suggested public text below.

emily: ```
We are currently investigating an issue causing elevated latency and errors for the embeddings API in US regions. Some requests may fail or take longer than expected. Our engineers are actively working on mitigation. We will update this status page within 30 minutes.
Affected: customers using embeddings in US regions
Impact: degraded response times and intermittent failed requests
```

raj: +1 to emily’s wording. From the infra side: we are seeing a GPU worker backlog on a small subset of hosts and one autoscaling group failing to scale past a limit due to a misconfigured max cap. We’re exercising fallback routing to other capacity now. Please do not publish that internal detail to customers.

kiara: tagging followups for ops handoff — I’m on the 10:30–13:30 shift and will own the next updates. @emily — I can send the 30m update once we have numbers.

legal-bot: Reminder: avoid definitive statements about data integrity until we've completed checks. Suggested clause: "We are continuing to validate whether any customer data was affected and will disclose confirmed findings."

maya: Good call, legal. Update draft incorporating changes below.

maya: ```
Investigating: We are investigating elevated latency and errors for the embeddings API in US regions. Some requests may fail or take longer than expected. Our engineers are actively working on mitigation and monitoring.
Affected: customers using embeddings in US regions
Impact: degraded response times and intermittent failed requests
Next update: within 30 minutes. We are validating whether any customer data was affected and will report confirmed findings.
```

dave: small nit — add timeframe when it started: "Started: 2026-03-15T10:05Z". Also recommend adding a monitored metric line so customers can see progress (e.g., error rate %).

emily: Nice. I’ll publish the initial "Investigating" update now with Maya’s latest wording + start time and the legal clause. I’ll use the "limited impact" severity for now.

emily: publishing in 3...2...1 :rocket:

incident-bot: Status page update published: "Investigating — embeddings API (US regions)" — https://status.redwood.example/incident/1955559999 (published 2026-03-15T10:22Z)

maya: Confirmed — initial update live. I’ll add a short internal note in the incident doc with observed error rate and host counts.

kiara: Taking point on the 30m check. If error rate drops <1% and no new 5xx for 10m, propose we move to "under investigation — recovering" wording for the next update.

raj: working on removing the scaling cap now; will post ETA in the thread once the patch is deployed (expect ~15 minutes).

maya: quick follow-up draft for the 30m update (if we’re still working):

maya: ```
Update (30 minutes): Engineers continue to mitigate elevated latency and errors for the embeddings API in US regions. We have put fallback routing in place and are deploying configuration fixes to restore full capacity. Some degradation may persist while capacity rebuilds. We will provide another update in 30 minutes or sooner.
```

emily: looks good. Add a single sentence at the top: "No confirmed customer data loss at this time; validation continues." (per legal guidance).

raj: patch applied to autoscaling cap; new instances joining. Rolling checks show error rate trending down from 8.2% -> 3.4% over last 5m.

maya: great. if trend continues I’ll draft a "recovering" update at +30m.

incident-bot: NOTE: scheduled update reminder at 2026-03-15T10:52Z (30m check).

-- (later) --

maya: Drafting resolved notice since error rate is <0.5% for 12m and autoscaling is stable. Please review before publishing.

maya: ```
Resolved: We have restored normal operation for the embeddings API in US regions. The issue, caused by a misconfigured autoscaling cap, was mitigated and capacity was restored. Impact: some requests may have failed or experienced elevated latency between 2026-03-15T10:05Z and 2026-03-15T10:40Z. No confirmed customer data loss at this time; validation completed and no data integrity issues found.

If you continue to see issues, please contact support and include affected request IDs and timestamps.
```

legal-bot: Approve the resolved wording but change "was caused by" to "was related to" to be cautious.

maya: updated and publishing resolved in 2 mins.

emily: publishing resolved now. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Status page update published: "Resolved — embeddings API (US regions)" — https://status.redwood.example/incident/1955559999/resolved (published 2026-03-15T10:44Z)

kiara: handing off ongoing monitoring to next shift. All good on my end.

maya: thanks all — excellent coordination. Closing this thread after adding final incident notes to the postmortem doc.
